brief.summary: A documentation-site builder for solo maintainers of small open-source projects who want reference docs without learning a static-site toolchain.
brief.user: Marcus Hale, a high-school chemistry teacher who in his spare time maintains a small open-source plugin that adds periodic-table lookups to a popular text editor. He codes fine but has never written structured docs, and this is his first evening using Quillstack.
brief.moment: He imported his plugin's README and wants to turn it into a proper reference: an install guide, a reference entry for each command, and a changelog. He got through the first-run setup, but his first preview build shows three broken cross-references. He doesn't understand why a note callout renders as plain text, and he isn't sure what the 'version' setting controls. He needs to learn just enough of the system to fix these and publish before he loses the evening.

prompt:
I need the front end for Quillstack. A documentation-site builder for solo maintainers of small open-source projects who want reference docs without learning a static-site toolchain.

Who's using it: Marcus Hale, a high-school chemistry teacher who in his spare time maintains a small open-source plugin that adds periodic-table lookups to a popular text editor. He codes fine but has never written structured docs, and this is his first evening using Quillstack.

What they're doing right now: He imported his plugin's README and wants to turn it into a proper reference: an install guide, a reference entry for each command, and a changelog. He got through the first-run setup, but his first preview build shows three broken cross-references. He doesn't understand why a note callout renders as plain text, and he isn't sure what the 'version' setting controls. He needs to learn just enough of the system to fix these and publish before he loses the evening.

What's in the system at this point: Project 'elemental.nvim', v0.9.2, 214 GitHub stars, MIT license. 11 pages drafted: Install, Quick Start, Configuration, 6 command references (:ElementLookup, :ElementMass, :ElementCompare, :Isotopes, :ElectronConfig, :Units), FAQ, Changelog. Build #1 results: 3 broken references (to 'config-options', 'units#molar', 'isotopes-table'), 1 callout written as '> NOTE:' instead of the supported syntax, and 2 warnings about missing page descriptions. Config file: site title, version '0.9', base URL unset. Setup checklist: 4 of 7 steps done (import, choose structure, name site, first build; still to do: fix warnings, set URL, publish). Help articles available on references, callouts, versioning and publishing.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
